<thought>From the spectrum we see a dominant monoisotopic peak with a modest M+1 peak (~5.6 % of base) and a very small M+2 peak (~0.5 %). The M+1 intensity is characteristic of the natural abundance of ^13C (≈1.1 % per carbon), indicating the presence of carbon. No other element shows a distinctive pattern at these relative intensities (e.g., Cl or Br would give a strong M+2 ≈ 30–50 %, which is absent). Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
